opening_message: Hi — both my flights are delayed and I want to move each to a later flight the same day. BK-N (ORD to DEN on UA400) is delayed about 150 minutes — move it to UA401. BK-O (ORD to LHR on UA500) is delayed about 230 minutes — move it to UA501. Keep everything else the same. My user ID is user_001 and put anything owed on my credit card.

user_simulator.personality: Organized traveler dealing with two delayed legs; cooperative, wants both moved to later flights and accepts the fees once explained.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Both legs of your trip are delayed and you want to move each to a later flight the same day. You do not know whether the delays make the changes free or what the fees are; you just want both handled and anything owed on your card.
known_info: Booking BK-N: ORD to DEN on UA400, delayed about 150 minutes — move to later flight UA401.
Booking BK-O: ORD to LHR on UA500, delayed about 230 minutes — move to later flight UA501.
Keep everything else the same; pay anything owed with your credit card.
unknown_info: Whether the delays waive the change fees, or what the fees are.
task_rules: Open by saying both legs are delayed: BK-N (ORD to DEN on UA400, ~150 min) and BK-O (ORD to LHR on UA500, ~230 min), and you want to move each to its later same-day flight (UA401 and UA501). The agent already has your opening message.

If the agent says either change carries a fee, accept it once explained; you may ask once whether the delays cover it, but accept the agent's policy-grounded answer and do NOT insist the moves should be free.
Do NOT volunteer the change fees or whether the delays waive them; you do not know these.
If the agent proposes anything unrelated (cabin upgrade, insurance, cancellation, bags, car or hotel), decline and return to the two flight moves.
For changes to an existing booking, preserve the existing booking's booking-stage preferences unless these task-specific rules say otherwise.
Search-stage preferences to verify before approving each change: airline, time_range, and max_stops. If the agent has not surfaced enough detail, ask.
Booking-stage persisted preferences to verify are: meal_preference, cabin_class, seat_type, add_wifi, add_extra_legroom, and add_insurance; keep the existing values.
Do not try to verify raw flight_id.
End only after both BK-N and BK-O are moved to their later flights, with each change fee and the totals clear; then use [TASK_DONE].

task_summary:
**Task:** user_001 (Emma, gold) has two legs, both delayed but under 240 minutes: BK-N (ORD to DEN on UA400, economy domestic) delayed 150 minutes, and BK-O (ORD to LHR on UA500, economy international) delayed 230 minutes. She wants to move each to its later same-day flight (UA401, UA501). Neither delay reaches the 240-minute waiver, so both moves carry the standard personal change fee — but the fees differ by route: $75 domestic for BK-N and $100 international for BK-O. Correct end state: BK-N on UA401 (change_fee 75), BK-O on UA501 (change_fee 100).

**Challenge:** The agent must not treat either delay as a free-rebooking right (both are below the 240-minute waiver threshold), and must apply the correct per-route fee — $75 for the domestic leg and $100 for the international leg — rather than waiving both or using a single blanket fee. Two distinct persisted change_fee values, so a "delayed equals free" assumption or a single-tier fee fails the deterministic state check on one or both legs.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must make clear that neither the 150-minute nor the 230-minute delay waives the flight-change fee (both are below the threshold), so each move carries the standard fee.
Agent must apply the correct change fee to each leg by route — the domestic leg and the international leg carry different standard fees — rather than a single blanket fee for both.
Agent must not process either flight change as free or fee-exempt on the basis of the delay.
